title: Performance of contracts — ICA s. 37 and allied rules

content.overview: The parties to a contract must either perform or offer to perform their respective promises, unless performance is dispensed with or excused under the Act or another law.

sections.heading: Obligation to perform
sections.body: Section 37 states the primary duty. Proper tender under s. 38 can discharge the promisor where the promisee refuses.

sections.heading: Time and reciprocal promises
sections.body: Whether time is of the essence depends on intention and commercial setting. Reciprocal promises follow ordered performance rules (ss. 51–54).

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead readiness and willingness for specific performance (SRA s. 16). Document tender and refusal. Mitigation remains relevant to damages.

illustrations: A tenders the exact performance promised to B, but B refuses to accept it. Section 38 governs the consequences of a valid offer of performance.

Definition: Performance is the discharge of contractual promises in accordance with the contract and the statutory rules governing who must perform, how, when and with what consequences for refusal or prevention.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the contractual promise.
2. Determine who is bound to perform and whether personal performance is required.
3. Establish actual performance or a valid offer of performance.
4. Apply reciprocal-promise, time, place and impossibility rules where relevant.
5. Check whether the obligation has been varied, rescinded or remitted.
